response.text:
# Selective EGFR Inhibitor Design for NSCLC Research

## 1. Target Validation

EGFR (UniProt **P00533**, gene `EGFR`, human, 1210 aa) was resolved and mapped to ChEMBL target **CHEMBL203** ("Epidermal growth factor receptor," single protein, *Homo sapiens*). I deliberately used the **single-protein target CHEMBL203** rather than the ErbB-family grouped targets (CHEMBL2111431, CHEMBL2363049) that were also returned — those pool EGFR with HER2/HER3/HER4 and would contaminate selectivity analysis with cross-family data.

A bioactivity pull against CHEMBL203 returned 230 activity rows / 161 unique molecules (IC50, Ki, Kd, EC50 types), with 94 dropped for missing pChEMBL and 76 censored values excluded, leaving a usable confident-affinity subset.

**Caveat on data completeness:** the `read_file` tool needed to pull the *full* activity table (beyond the ~200-row/preview slice shown by the tool call) was unavailable in this session ("no tool named read_file"), so the analysis below is built from the **preview rows actually visible in the tool output**, not the complete 161-molecule set. Any SAR trend stated here should be treated as directional, not a validated quantitative model — a follow-up pull with full pagination is needed before this goes further.

## 2. What the visible data shows

Two exemplar molecules were visible in the returned preview:

| ChEMBL ID | SMILES | Type | Value | pChEMBL |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| CHEMBL336264 | `C=CS(=O)(=O)c1cc2c(Nc3cccc(Br)c3)ncnc2cn1` | IC50 | 0.43 nM | 9.37 |
| CHEMBL304271 | `CCN(CC)CC(O)CNC(=O)c1cc(C)c(/C=C2\C(=O)Nc3ncnc(Nc4ccc(F)c(Cl)c4)c32)[nH]1` | IC50 | (value truncated in preview) | — |

CHEMBL336264 is a quinazoline/pyrrolopyrimidine-type scaffold bearing a vinyl sulfone — a **Michael-acceptor covalent warhead**, structurally in the family of 3rd-generation covalent EGFR inhibitors (osimertinib-class chemistry, which targets the Cys797 residue near the ATP pocket to achieve potency and mutant selectivity, e.g. for T790M). CHEMBL304271 resembles an aniline-substituted indolinone/quinazolinone with a solubilizing diethylaminopropanol tail — more reminiscent of earlier reversible EGFR chemotypes (gefitinib/erlotinib-era anilinoquinazolines).
